summary: The reflog is a local record of every commit HEAD has pointed to. It lets you find and restore commits that a reset or a deleted branch removed from the log.
notes: HEAD@{0} is where you are now, HEAD@{1} is one move earlier, and so on.
git branch rescue HEAD@{1} is another way to recover: it puts a new branch on the lost commit.
The reflog is only on your computer, and Git deletes old entries after about 90 days.
pitfall: The reflog only has commits. Changes you never committed are not in it, so git reset --hard on uncommitted work cannot be undone.
setup_note: Starts in a repository with three commits on main.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz scores for Period 3.
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add gradebook script"

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add quiz scores"
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Print a letter grade"
